claim: Transcription factors called terminal selectors activate identity-specific effector genes during neuronal differentiation to define the structural and functional properties of a neuron.
source: Transcription factors called terminal selectors activate identity-specific effector genes during neuronal differentiation to define the structural and functional properties of a neuron.
evidence: This is a foundational statement in the abstract that draws from established scientific knowledge about terminal selectors and is supported by citations throughout the manuscript.

claim: In undifferentiated cells, ectopic expression of CHE-1 results in activation of ASE neuron type-specific effector genes.
source: In undifferentiated cells, ectopic expression of CHE-1 results in activation of ASE neuron type-specific effector genes.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 1 showing broad activation of gcy-5 in early embryos.

claim: Once cells differentiate, their plasticity is restricted and ectopic expression of CHE-1 no longer results in activation of ASE effector genes.
source: Once cells differentiate, their plasticity is restricted and ectopic expression of CHE-1 no longer results in activation of ASE effector genes.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 1 showing reduced activation of gcy-5 when CHE-1 is induced at later developmental stages.

claim: Removal of terminal selectors of other sensory, inter-, or motor neuron types enables ectopically expressed CHE-1 to activate its ASE-specific effector genes.
source: In striking contrast, removal of the respective terminal selectors of other sensory, inter-, or motor neuron types now enables ectopically expressed CHE-1 to activate its ASE-specific effector genes, indicating that terminal selectors not only activate effector gene batteries but also control the restriction of cellular plasticity.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figures 2 and 3 showing increased activation of ASE markers in various terminal selector mutants.

claim: Terminal selectors not only activate effector gene batteries but also control the restriction of cellular plasticity.
source: In striking contrast, removal of the respective terminal selectors of other sensory, inter-, or motor neuron types now enables ectopically expressed CHE-1 to activate its ASE-specific effector genes, indicating that terminal selectors not only activate effector gene batteries but also control the restriction of cellular plasticity.
evidence: This is a key conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing that terminal selector mutants retain plasticity.

claim: Terminal selectors mediate restriction of plasticity at least partially by organizing chromatin.
source: Terminal selectors mediate this restriction at least partially by organizing chromatin.
evidence: This is supported by the LacO/LacI spot assay data in Figure 5 showing changes in chromatin compaction in unc-3 mutants.

claim: The chromatin structure of a CHE-1 target locus is less compact in neurons that lack their resident terminal selector.
source: The chromatin structure of a CHE-1 target locus is less compact in neurons that lack their resident terminal selector and genetic epistasis studies with H3K9 methyltransferases suggest that this chromatin modification acts downstream of a terminal selector to restrict plasticity.
evidence: This is directly supported by the LacO/LacI spot assay data in Figure 5E showing larger GFP spots in unc-3 mutants.

claim: H3K9 methylation acts downstream of a terminal selector to restrict plasticity.
source: The chromatin structure of a CHE-1 target locus is less compact in neurons that lack their resident terminal selector and genetic epistasis studies with H3K9 methyltransferases suggest that this chromatin modification acts downstream of a terminal selector to restrict plasticity.
evidence: This is supported by genetic epistasis data in Figure 6B showing that met-2 set-25 double mutants do not enhance the unc-3 phenotype.

claim: Terminal selectors activate identity-specific genes and make non-identity-defining genes less accessible.
source: Taken together, terminal selectors activate identity-specific genes and make non-identity-defining genes less accessible, thereby serving as a checkpoint to coordinate identity specification with restriction of cellular plasticity.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from all the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Terminal selectors serve as a checkpoint to coordinate identity specification with restriction of cellular plasticity.
source: Taken together, terminal selectors activate identity-specific genes and make non-identity-defining genes less accessible, thereby serving as a checkpoint to coordinate identity specification with restriction of cellular plasticity.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, synthesizing all experimental findings.

claim: When nuclei from progressively more differentiated frog intestinal cells were transplanted into enucleated eggs, egg cells containing less differentiated nuclei developed into tadpoles more efficiently than eggs containing more differentiated nuclei.
source: When nuclei from progressively more differentiated frog intestinal cells were transplanted into enucleated eggs, it was observed that egg cells containing less differentiated nuclei developed into tadpoles more efficiently than eggs containing more differentiated nuclei (Gurdon, 1960, 1962).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Gurdon's pioneering work.

claim: The overexpression of myogenic helix-loop-helix TF hlh-1/MyoD early in embryonic development leads to the activation of muscle genes in all somatic cells in C. elegans.
source: For instance, in C. elegans, the overexpression of myogenic helix-loop-helix TF hlh-1/MyoD early in embryonic development leads to the activation of muscle genes in all somatic cells (Fukushige and Krause, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Fukushige and Krause, 2005.

claim: The ability of hlh-1 to activate its target genes decreases and is completely lost by the time the embryonic cells are post-mitotic.
source: However, the ability of hlh-1 to activate its target genes decreases and is completely lost by the time the embryonic cells are post-mitotic.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Fukushige and Krause, 2005 in the preceding sentence.

claim: The overexpression of pluripotency TFs c-Myc, Klf4, Sox2, and Oct4 in non-terminally differentiated Pro-B cells leads to the formation of iPSCs, but expression in differentiated B lymphocytes does not.
source: Likewise, the overexpression of pluripotency TFs c-Myc, Klf4, Sox2, and Oct4 in non-terminally differentiated Pro-B cells leads to the formation of iPSCs, but expression in differentiated B lymphocytes does not (Hanna et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Hanna et al., 2008.

claim: Electron microscopy shows mostly open euchromatin in cells of early embryos and an accumulation of closed heterochromatic regions in differentiated cells in C. elegans and mice.
source: In C. elegans and mice, electron microscopy shows mostly open euchromatin in cells of early embryos and an accumulation of closed heterochromatic regions in differentiated cells (Efroni et al., 2008; Leung et al., 1999; Park et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Efroni et al., 2008; Leung et al., 1999; Park et al., 2004.

claim: H3K27me3 is enriched on developmentally regulated, cell-type-specific genes.
source: H3K27me3 is enriched on developmentally regulated, cell-type-specific genes (Boyer et al., 2006; Filion et al., 2010; Ho et al., 2014; Oktaba et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Boyer et al., 2006; Filion et al., 2010; Ho et al., 2014; Oktaba et al., 2008.

claim: The depletion of H3K27me3 in embryos leads to an extension of the time during which chromatin stays more 'open' and a correlated increase in the window of time during which an ectopically expressed TF, pha-4, can activate its target genes in embryonic cells.
source: The depletion of H3K27me3 in embryos leads to an extension of the time during which chromatin stays more 'open' and a correlated increase in the window of time during which an ectopically expressed TF, pha-4, can activate its target genes in embryonic cells (Yuzyuk et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Yuzyuk et al., 2009.

claim: Loss of H3K27me3 depositing polycomb repressive complex 2 (PRC2) in the germ cells of C. elegans leads to a gain of plasticity, as measured by the ability of three different identity-specifying TFs to activate their target genes.
source: In previous studies, we have also shown that loss of H3K27me3 depositing polycomb repressive complex 2 (PRC2) in the germ cells of C. elegans leads to a gain of plasticity, as measured by the ability of three different identity-specifying TFs to activate their target genes (Patel et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Patel et al., 2012.

claim: H3K9me3 is enriched at repeat-rich regions which remain repressed in all cell types.
source: On the other hand, H3K9me3 is enriched at repeat-rich regions which remain repressed in all cell types, but there is accumulating evidence that it is also involved in the repression of cell-type-specific genes (Allan et al., 2012; Feldman et al., 2006; Garrigues et al., 2015; Ho et al., 2014; Loh et al., 2007; Martens et al., 2005; Towbin et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Allan et al., 2012; Feldman et al., 2006; Garrigues et al., 2015; Ho et al., 2014; Loh et al., 2007; Martens et al., 2005; Towbin et al., 2012.

claim: Removing methyl transferases that deposit H3K9me3 increases the efficiency of fibroblast to iPSC reprogramming.
source: As for restricting plasticity, it has been observed that removing methyl transferases that deposit H3K9me3 increases the efficiency of fibroblast to iPSC reprogramming (Soufi et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Soufi et al., 2012.

claim: H3K9me3 is enriched at targets of iPSC-inducing 'Yamanaka' factors that fail to become activated in fibroblasts that do not convert into iPSCs.
source: Furthermore, H3K9me3 is enriched at targets of iPSC-inducing 'Yamanaka' factors that fail to become activated in fibroblasts that do not convert into iPSCs (Soufi et al., 2012; Soufi and Zaret, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Soufi et al., 2012; Soufi and Zaret, 2013.

claim: CHE-1 is a Zn-finger TF which is normally only expressed in two glutamatergic ASE sensory neurons.
source: To assay restriction, we have used the overexpression of terminal selector CHE-1, a Zn-finger TF, which is normally only expressed in two glutamatergic ASE sensory neurons and which specifies the identity of these neurons by activating expression of ASE-specific genes (Etchberger et al., 2007; Patel et al., 2012; Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013; Uchida et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Etchberger et al., 2007; Patel et al., 2012; Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013; Uchida et al., 2003.

claim: CHE-1 specifies the identity of ASE neurons by activating expression of ASE-specific genes.
source: To assay restriction, we have used the overexpression of terminal selector CHE-1, a Zn-finger TF, which is normally only expressed in two glutamatergic ASE sensory neurons and which specifies the identity of these neurons by activating expression of ASE-specific genes (Etchberger et al., 2007; Patel et al., 2012; Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013; Uchida et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Etchberger et al., 2007; Patel et al., 2012; Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013; Uchida et al., 2003.

claim: unc-3 is a COE (Collier/Olf1/Ebf) TF which specifies the identity of cholinergic motor neurons.
source: To understand the mechanistic basis of the plasticity-restricting function of terminal selectors, we focused on unc-3, a COE (Collier/Olf1/Ebf) TF which specifies the identity of cholinergic motor neurons (MNs).
evidence: This claim is supported by the context and citations in the manuscript (Kratsios et al., 2011; Prasad et al., 1998).

claim: When CHE-1hs is induced during early embryonic stages (<300 min), gcy-5prom::gfp is broadly activated in numerous cells.
source: When CHE-1hs is induced during early embryonic stages (<300 min), gcy-5prom::gfp is broadly activated in numerous cells (Figure 1Aiii).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1Aiii.

claim: Induction of CHE-1hs during larval development results in an increasingly restricted activation of gcy-5.
source: Induction of CHE-1hs during larval development results in an increasingly restricted activation of gcy-5, and the animals retain a normal overall morphology (Figure 1Aiv–viii).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1Aiv-viii.

claim: Cells that express gcy-5 in response to larval CHE-1hs are those that have just been generated and hence are still differentiating.
source: With the exception of a few neurons in the head and tail, cells that express gcy-5 in response to larval CHE-1hs are those that have just been generated and hence are still differentiating (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: CHE-1hs induction in the L2/L3 stage activates gcy-5 in seam cells and ventral nerve cord (VNC) neurons, which are dividing and differentiating at this time.
source: For instance, CHE-1hs induction in the L2/L3 stage activates gcy-5 in seam cells and ventral nerve cord (VNC) neurons, which are dividing and differentiating at this time.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and observations in the manuscript.

claim: Activation of gcy-5fosmid::gfp after L2 CHE-1hs expression is enriched in rab-3low cells.
source: In these worms, activation of gcy-5fosmid::gfp after L2 CHE-1hs expression is enriched in rab-3low cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A), showing that cells that are dividing and differentiating are more receptive to CHE-1 than cells that have already differentiated.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Vulval muscle cells, which are dividing and differentiating at the L3 stage, are receptive to CHE-1hs at this stage.
source: We also observe that vulval muscle cells, which are dividing and differentiating at the L3 stage are receptive to CHE-1hs at this stage (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: At the L4 and adult stages, when all tissues have differentiated, the only cells that activate gcy-5prom::gfp in response to CHE-1hs are a handful of neurons and pharyngeal muscle cells.
source: At the L4 and adult stages, when all tissues have differentiated, the only cells that activate gcy-5prom::gfp in response to CHE-1hs are a handful of neurons and pharyngeal muscle cells, suggesting that these differentiated cells provide some molecular context which makes them amenable to che-1 activity (Figure 1Aviii and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1Aviii and B.

claim: The CHE-1 responsive neurons include the RIS, CEP, ASK, and ASI neurons.
source: The CHE-1 responsive neurons include the RIS, CEP, ASK, and ASI neurons.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental data.

claim: Expression of gcy-5prom::gfp overlaps with the expression of endogenous gcy-5 mRNA, indicating that the endogenous gcy-5 gene is induced by ectopic CHE-1hs.
source: Additionally, gcy-5 smFISH of these worms shows that expression of gcy-5prom::gfp overlaps with the expression of endogenous gcy-5 mRNA, indicating that the endogenous gcy-5 gene is induced by ectopic CHE-1hs and that the transgene gcy-5prom::gfp reliably replicates the activity of the endogenous gcy-5 locus (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: After heatshock induction in adults, both che-1 mRNA and protein can be detected in all cell types.
source: Ater heatshock induction in adults, both che-1 mRNA and protein can be detected in all cell types (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C,D.

claim: A synthetic strong reporter that contains a 4X multimerized CHE-1 binding site is expressed broadly, in all somatic cell types at every stage of development, in response to CHE-1hs expression.
source: We find that this gcy-54XASE::gfp reporter is expressed broadly, in all somatic cell types at every stage of development, in response to CHE-1hs expression from both the multi-copy and single-copy heatshock-inducible transgenes (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: If CHE-1hs is induced during early embryonic stages, the resulting arrested embryos and larvae activate broad expression of gcy-6fosmid::gfp and gcy-7prom::rfp.
source: If CHE-1hs is induced during early embryonic stages, the resulting arrested embryos and larvae activate broad expression of gcy-6fosmid::gfp and gcy-7prom::rfp.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Expression of gcy-6 and gcy-7 markers becomes more restricted as CHE-1hs is induced at later stages.
source: Expression of these markers also becomes more restricted as CHE-1hs is induced at later stages.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Ectopic induction of gcy-6 and gcy-7 is not as broad as gcy-5 and no ectopic expression is detected when CHE-1hs is induced in larval stages.
source: However, ectopic induction of these genes is not as broad as gcy-5 and no ectopic expression is detected when CHE-1hs is induced in larval stages. (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: CHE-1 is sufficient to activate ASER-specific genes, but may require other co-activators to activate ASEL-specific genes.
source: Previous analysis has shown that while CHE-1 is sufficient to activate ASER-specific genes, it may require other co-activators to activate ASEL-specific genes (Etchberger et al., 2009; Hobert, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Etchberger et al., 2009; Hobert, 2014.

claim: CHE-1 driven by all neuronal promoters resulted in broad ectopic expression of gcy-5prom::gfp, gcy-5fosmid::gfp, and ceh-36fosmid::yfp.
source: CHE-1 driven by all neuronal promoters resulted in broad ectopic expression of gcy-5prom::gfp, gcy-5fosmid::gfp, and ceh-36fosmid::yfp (another che-1 target, a homeodomain TF expressed in ASEL/R and AWC neurons) .
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A.

claim: gcy-6fosmid::gfp and gcy-7prom::rfp show restricted activation in only 1–2 extra cells when CHE-1 is driven by neuronal promoters.
source: However, gcy-6fosmid::gfp and gcy-7prom::rfp show restricted activation in only 1–2 extra cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A.

claim: Transgenic animals expressing CHE-1 in the hypodermis or muscle showed gcy-5prom::gfp expression in the respective tissues.
source: Transgenic animals expressing CHE-1 in the hypodermis or muscle also showed gcy-5prom::gfp expression in the respective tissues (Figure 1—figure supplement 3b,c).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3b,c.

claim: A wide range of cell types are receptive to CHE-1 activity after post-mitotic division while they are terminally differentiating.
source: In combination with the heatshock experiments, these experiments show that a wide range of cell types are receptive to CHE-1 activity after post-mitotic division while they are terminally differentiating.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data in Figure 1 and related supplements.

claim: Once terminal differentiation is accomplished, most cells lose their multipotency and become refractory to CHE-1 activity.
source: Once terminal differentiation is accomplished, most cells lose their multipotency and become refractory to CHE-1 activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data in Figure 1.

claim: unc-3(-) cholinergic MNs are born and found in approximately their wildtype positions in the ventral nerve cord (VNC), retro-vesicular ganglion (RVG), and pre-anal ganglion (PAG) of the worm.
source: unc-3(-) cholinergic MNs are born and found in approximately their wildtype positions in the ventral nerve cord (VNC), retro-vesicular ganglion (RVG), and pre-anal ganglion (PAG) of the worm.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Kratsios et al., 2011; Prasad et al., 1998.

claim: unc-3(-) cholinergic MNs express pan-neuronal identity markers, and form axonal projections.
source: They express pan-neuronal identity markers, and form axonal projections.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Kratsios et al., 2011; Prasad et al., 1998.

claim: unc-3(-) cholinergic MNs lack expression of all the acetylcholine pathway genes, numerous other terminal identity genes, show defects in synaptogenesis and are non-functional.
source: However, these neurons lack expression of all the acetylcholine pathway genes, numerous other terminal identity genes, show defects in synaptogenesis and are non-functional (Kratsios et al., 2011; Prasad et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Kratsios et al., 2011; Prasad et al., 1998.

claim: In wildtype worms, an average of 11 neurons activate gcy-5prom::gfp at the L2 stage upon ectopic CHE-1hs expression, and this number is reduced to an average of 2 neurons by the L4 and adult stages.
source: In wildtype worms, we find that an average of 11 neurons activate gcy-5prom::gfp at the L2 stage upon ectopic CHE-1hs expression, and this number is reduced to an average of 2 neurons by the L4 and adult stages.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: In unc-3 mutants, a significantly higher number of neurons express gcy-5prom::gfp at every developmental stage upon ectopic CHE-1hs expression.
source: In unc-3 mutants, a significantly higher number of neurons express gcy-5prom::gfp at every developmental stage upon ectopic CHE-1hs expression (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: gcy-5prom::gfp expression in the VNC was not seen when unc-3 mutants were heatshocked in the absence of the hsprom::che-1 transgene.
source: gcy-5prom::gfp expression in the VNC was not seen when unc-3 mutants were heatshocked in the absence of the hsprom::che-1 transgene, showing that the loss of unc-3 is not sufficient for an identity switch.
evidence: This is a control experiment demonstrating that unc-3 loss alone does not activate gcy-5.

claim: Expression of endogenous gcy-5 mRNA was induced in unc-3(-) cells to a similar extent as the gcy-5prom::gfp reporter.
source: Additionally, smFISH of these worms showed that expression of endogenous gcy-5 mRNA was also induced in unc-3(-) cells to a similar extent (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: About 30% of affected neurons in unc-3 mutants express gcy-5 in response to CHE-1hs induction.
source: On average, about 30% of affected neurons in unc-3 mutants express gcy-5 in response to CHE-1hs induction.
evidence: This is a quantification of the experimental data.

claim: Genes that showed increased induction after L4 CHE-1hs in unc-3 included the glutamate transporter eat-4fosmid::yfp, the homeodomain TF ceh-36fosmid::yfp, and the ciliary protein ift-20prom::rfp.
source: Genes that showed increased induction after L4 CHE-1hs in unc-3 included the glutamate transporter eat-4fosmid::yfp, the homeodomain TF ceh-36fosmid::yfp, and the ciliary protein ift-20prom::rfp (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: No induction of gcy-6fosmid::gfp or gcy-7prom::rfp was observed in wildtype or unc-3(-) neurons.
source: No induction of gcy-6fosmid::gfp or gcy-7prom::rfp was observed in wildtype or unc-3(-) neurons, which is consistent with the idea that che-1 is not sufficient for the induction of these genes, as discussed earlier (0 neurons induced in >20 worms checked).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: Neither unc-4 mutants, nor unc-55; mab-9 double mutants show increased induction of gcy-5prom::gfp in cholinergic MNs in response to CHE-1hs.
source: Neither unc-4 mutants, nor unc-55; mab-9 double mutants, however, show increased induction of gcy-5prom::gfp in cholinergic MNs in response to CHE-1hs (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: A disruption of function and identity-specific transcriptional programs does not automatically make cells more plastic.
source: These data demonstrate that a disruption of function and identity-specific transcriptional programs does not automatically make cells more plastic.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the unc-4 and unc-55; mab-9 mutant data.

claim: 30% of ets-5(-) BAG neurons express gcy-5fosmid::gfp in response to adult CHE-1hs as opposed to 4% of wildtype BAG neurons.
source: Specifically, ets-5 is a terminal selector for the CO2 sensing BAG neurons (Guillermin et al., 2011). In our assay, 30% of ets-5(-) BAG neurons express gcy-5fosmid::gfp in response to adult CHE-1hs as opposed to 4% of wildtype BAG neurons (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A and citation to Guillermin et al., 2011.

claim: 23% of ttx-1(-) AFD neurons express gcy-5fosmid::gfp after adult CHE-1hs whereas 2% of wildtype AFD neurons do.
source: ttx-1 is a terminal selector for thermosensory AFD neurons (Satterlee et al., 2001; Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013) and 23% of ttx-1(-) AFD neurons express gcy-5fosmid::gfp after adult CHE-1hs whereas 2% of wildtype AFD neurons do (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B and citations to Satterlee et al., 2001; Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013.

claim: Removing both ttx-1 and ceh-14 results in 34.3% of AFD neurons expressing gcy-5fosmid::gfp compared to 4.8% in matched wildtypes.
source: Removing both ttx-1 and ceh-14, the co-factor of ttx-1 in AFD specification, results in a 34.3% phenotype compared to 4.8% in matched wildtypes.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: An average increase of five gcy-5fosmid-positive neurons is found in the tails of ceh-14 mutants upon CHE-1 induction.
source: ceh-14 also acts as a terminal selector in several distinct tail neuron classes (Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013). We found an average increase of five gcy-5fosmid-positive neurons in the tails of ceh-14 mutants upon CHE-1 induction (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C and citation to Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013.

claim: 30% of lin-11(-) ASG neurons express gcy-5fosmid::gfp as opposed to 2% of wildtype ASG neurons.
source: Lastly, lin-11 is required for terminal identity specification of ASG neurons (Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013), and 30% of lin-11(-) ASG neurons express gcy-5fosmid::gfp as opposed to 2% of wildtype ASG neurons (Figure 3d).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3d and citation to Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013.

claim: No increases in induction of gcy-5prom::gfp or ceh-36fosmid::yfp were detected in response to CHE-1hs in the GABAergic MNs of unc-30.
source: unc-30 is the terminal selector for GABAergic MNs in the VNC and unc-42 is the terminal selector for ASH sensory neurons (Baran et al., 1999; Cinar et al., 2005; Jin et al., 1994; Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013). No increases in induction of gcy-5prom::gfp or ceh-36fosmid::yfp were detected in response to CHE-1hs in the GABAergic MNs of unc-30 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, data only shown for ceh-36fosmid::yfp).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and citations to Baran et al., 1999; Cinar et al., 2005; Jin et al., 1994; Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013.

claim: Neither gcy-5fosmid::rfp, nor ceh-36fosmid::yfp was detected in the ASH neurons of unc-42 mutants after CHE-1 misexpression.
source: In the case of unc-42 mutants, neither gcy-5fosmid::rfp, nor ceh-36fosmid::yfp was detected in the ASH neurons after CHE-1 misexpression (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D, data only shown for gcy-5fosmid::rfp).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Expression of che-1 early in the development of GABAergic MNs and ASH neurons leads to activation of target genes.
source: Expression of che-1 early in the development of GABAergic MNs and ASH neurons does lead to activation of target genes, based on tissue-specific promoter driven expression of che-1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Activation of CHE-1hs in L4s/adults results in the expression of gcy-54XASE::gfp in both GABAergic MNs and ASH neurons.
source: Additionally, activation of CHE-1hs in L4s/adults results in the expression of gcy-54XASE::gfp in both sets of neurons (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E,F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E,F.

claim: While unc-30 and unc-42 are required for terminal differentiation, they are dispensable for restricting cellular plasticity.
source: Therefore, we conclude that while unc-30 and unc-42 are required for terminal differentiation, they are dispensable for restricting cellular plasticity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on unc-30 and unc-42 mutants.

claim: The loss of a terminal identity in itself is not sufficient to keep a neuron in a plastic state.
source: The negative results with unc-30 and unc-42 demonstrate that the loss of a terminal identity in itself it not sufficient to keep a neuron in a plastic state.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on unc-30 and unc-42 mutants.

claim: The restriction of plasticity is a distinct and parallel function carried out by certain terminal selector TFs.
source: This suggests that the restriction of plasticity is a distinct and parallel function carried out by certain terminal selector TFs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the differential effects of various terminal selector mutants.

claim: The unc-3::mNG::AID allele displays wildtype locomotion and expresses cholinergic MN markers at near wildtype levels in the absence of TIR1 and auxin.
source: In the absence of TIR1 and auxin, the unc-3::mNG::AID worms display wildtype locomotion and express cholinergic MN markers at near wildtype levels (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: Cholinergic MNs of unc-3::mNG::AID worms were receptive to CHE-1hs, even in the absence of TIR1 and auxin.
source: However, cholinergic MNs of these worms were receptive to CHE-1hs, even in the absence of TIR1 and auxin (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C,D.

claim: When CHE-1hs is overexpressed in adult worms containing unc-3::mNG::AID, expression of gcy-5prom::gfp is observed at a penetrance indistinguishable from that observed in the unc-3 null allele.
source: When CHE-1hs is overexpressed in adult worms containing unc-3::mNG::AID, expression of gcy-5prom::gfp is observed at a penetrance indistinguishable from that observed in the unc-3 null allele.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: In the unc-3::mNG::AID allele, cholinergic MNs differentiate largely normally, and yet retain plasticity in response to CHE-1hs activity.
source: Hence, in this allele the cholinergic MNs differentiate largely normally, and yet retain plasticity in response to CHE-1hs activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on the unc-3::mNG::AID allele.

claim: Terminal selector TFs control restriction independently of specification.
source: This allele therefore supports the hypothesis that terminal selector-like TFs control restriction independently of specification.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the unc-3::mNG::AID allele data.

claim: The ace-2 LacO array is transcriptionally active in wildtype cholinergic neurons but not in unc-3 mutants.
source: The ace-2 LacO array is transcriptionally active in wildtype cholinergic neurons but not in unc-3 mutants (Figure 5B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B,C.

claim: The ace-2 LacO array showed a significantly higher GFP pixel count in wildtype VNC neurons as compared to unc-3.
source: Consistent with its expression, the ace-2 LacO array showed a significantly higher GFP pixel count in wildtype VNC neurons as compared to unc-3 (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C,D.

claim: The size of the GFP spot on the gcy-5 LacO array was increased in unc-3 mutant MNs compared to wildtype.
source: We then quantified GFP spots on the LacO array that contains gcy-5, the ASE-specific CHE-1 target gene that is normally not expressed in VNC MNs. In this case, the size of the GFP spot was increased in unc-3 mutant MNs compared to wildtype (Figure 5E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The gcy-5 locus is in a less compact state in unc-3 mutant cholinergic MNs, which may make it more amenable to activation by CHE-1.
source: These data show that the gcy-5 locus is in a less compact state in unc-3 mutant cholinergic MNs, which may make it more amenable to activation by CHE-1.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the LacO/LacI spot assay data.

claim: The size of the gcy-5 LacO array in hypodermal cells of wildtype and unc-3 mutants show no statistically significant difference.
source: If the change in compaction of the gcy-5 array were caused by unc-3 function, this change should be specific to neurons in which unc-3 acts as a terminal selector. Indeed, the size of the gcy-5 LacO array in hypodermal cells of wildtype and unc-3 mutants show no statistically significant difference (Figure 5F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Loss of mes-2 permits CHE-1hs to induce gcy-5prom::gfp to the same extent as removal of unc-3 does.
source: We found that loss of mes-2 permits CHE-1hs to induce gcy-5prom::gfp to the same extent as removal of unc-3 does (Figure 6A), indicating that mes-2 is indeed required for restriction of plasticity in cholinergic MNs.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Removal of both unc-3 and mes-2 leads to the induction of gcy-5prom::gfp in twice as many cells as seen in unc-3 or mes-2 mutants alone.
source: To determine whether mes-2 acts in parallel or in the same pathway as unc-3, we tested mes-2; unc-3 double mutants and found that they have an additive phenotype. Removal of both unc-3 and mes-2 leads to the induction of gcy-5prom::gfp in twice as many cells as seen in unc-3 or mes-2 mutants alone.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: unc-3 and mes-2 work in parallel genetic pathways to ensure plasticity restriction in differentiated cholinergic MNs.
source: This suggests that unc-3 and mes-2 work in parallel genetic pathways to ensure plasticity restriction in differentiated cholinergic MNs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the additive phenotype of mes-2; unc-3 double mutants.

claim: Both met-2 and set-25 mutants have significantly more gcy-5prom::gfp expressing cholinergic MNs compared to wildtype.
source: Both met-2 and set-25 mutants have significantly more gcy-5prom::gfp expressing cholinergic MNs compared to wildtype.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: For set-25 the increase in gcy-5prom::gfp expression is only modest, and a met-2 set-25 double mutant is not significantly different from met-2.
source: However, for set-25 the increase is only modest, and a met-2 set-25 double mutant is not significantly different from met-2, suggesting met-2, has a greater role in making the gcy-5prom::gfp locus inaccessible to CHE-1.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: An additive phenotype is not evident in met-2; unc-3, set-25; unc-3, or met-2 set-25; unc-3, suggesting that these factors might act in the same pathway to restrict the accessibility of gcy-5prom::gfp.
source: An additive phenotype is not evident in met-2; unc-3, set-25; unc-3, or met-2 set-25; unc-3, suggesting that these factors might act in the same pathway to restrict the accessibility of gcy-5prom::gfp.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: met-2; set-25 double mutants lack H3K9me3 at the L4 and adult stages.
source: Using antibody staining, we ensured that met-2; set-25 double mutants also lack H3K9me3 at the L4 and adult stages where we perform our experiments (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Induction of CHE-1hs leads to increased activation of gcy-5prom::gfp in the cholinergic MNs of met-2 single mutants and met-2 set-25 double mutants, but not in set-25 single mutants.
source: We found that induction of CHE-1hs does lead to increased activation of gcy-5prom::gfp in the cholinergic MNs of met-2 single mutants and met-2 set-25 double mutants, but not in set-25 single mutants (Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: H3K9me1/2 and H3K9me3 have to be perturbed for CHE-1hs to activate gcy-5prom::gfp.
source: This suggests that H3K9me1/2 and H3K9me3 have to be perturbed for CHE-1hs to activate gcy-5prom::gfp.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the met-2 and set-25 mutant data.

claim: The loss of met-2; set-25 in transgenic worms containing the single copy hs::che-1 transgene results in the expression of gcy-5prom::gfp in the cholinergic MNs.
source: To ensure that our phenotype is not an artifact of repetitive transgenes, we confirmed that the loss of met-2; set-25 in transgenic worms containing the single copy hs::che-1 transgene also results in the expression of gcy-5prom::gfp in the cholinergic MNs and that the expression of gfp in these worms overlaps with gcy-5 mRNA expression as determined by smFISH of endogenous gcy-5 transcripts (Figure 6E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: None of the met-2;unc-3, set-25;unc-3 and met-2 set-25;unc-3 double and triple mutants show an additive effect that is significantly different from the phenotype of unc-3 single mutants.
source: None of these double and triple mutants show an additive effect that is significantly different from the phenotype of unc-3 single mutants (Figure 6B), indicating that met-2, set-25, and unc-3 act in the same pathway rather than in parallel pathways.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: met-2, set-25, and unc-3 act in the same pathway rather than in parallel pathways.
source: None of these double and triple mutants show an additive effect that is significantly different from the phenotype of unc-3 single mutants (Figure 6B), indicating that met-2, set-25, and unc-3 act in the same pathway rather than in parallel pathways.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the genetic epistasis data.

claim: met-2;set-25 dependent H3K9 methylation is not the only pathway affected in the unc-3 mutants.
source: Since the removal of met-2 and set-25 does not result in as strong a phenotype as an unc-3 single mutant, we furthermore infer that met-2;set-25 dependent H3K9 methylation is not the only pathway affected in the unc-3 mutants.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing the phenotypes of met-2 set-25 and unc-3 mutants.

claim: An increased induction of gcy-5prom::gfp was seen in MNs after removal of both hpl-1 and hpl-2, and this phenotype was enhanced in the double mutant.
source: Indeed, an increased induction of gcy-5prom::gfp was seen in MNs after removal of both hpl-1 and hpl-2, and this phenotype was enhanced in the double mutant, so that it was stronger than the phenotype of met-2 set-25 mutants (Figure 6c).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6c.

claim: An hpl-2; hpl-1 unc-3 triple mutant shows a phenotype that is enhanced from the hpl-1; hpl-2 double or the unc-3 mutant alone, but it is not completely additive.
source: An hpl-2; hpl-1 unc-3 triple mutant also shows a phenotype that is enhanced from the hpl-1; hpl-2 double or the unc-3 mutant alone, but it is not completely additive.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6c.

claim: HP1 has functions independent of met-2 set-25 and H3K9me.
source: This enhancement indicates that HP1 has functions independent of met-2 set-25 and H3K9me.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the hpl-1; hpl-2; unc-3 triple mutant data.

claim: Induction of gcy-5 in all of the mutants tested required CHE-1hs induction.
source: Induction of gcy-5 in all of the mutants tested here required CHE-1hs induction.
evidence: This is a control observation confirming that the phenotypes are dependent on CHE-1 activity.

claim: Both H3K9me and H3K27me contribute to the restriction of plasticity in differentiated cells.
source: Taken together, both H3K9me and H3K27me contribute to the restriction of plasticity in differentiated cells.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the chromatin modifier mutant data.

claim: H3K9me might be acting along with terminal selectors to mediate restriction of plasticity, while H3K27me acts in parallel.
source: H3K9me might be acting along with terminal selectors to mediate this process, while H3K27me acts in parallel (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the genetic epistasis data.

claim: Terminal selector mutant neurons can retain plasticity even if they are not in a progenitor-like state.
source: In contrast, we find that terminal selector-mutant cells can retain plasticity even if they are not in a progenitor-like state.
evidence: This is a key conclusion distinguishing this work from previous studies.

claim: Terminal selector mutant neurons are postmitotic, still adopt a neuronal morphology, and normally activate expression of pan-neuronal features such as presynaptic vesicle machinery.
source: They are postmitotic, still adopt a neuronal morphology, and normally activate expression of pan-neuronal features such as presynaptic vesicle machinery (Cassata et al., 2000; Etchberger et al., 2007; Kratsios et al., 2011; Stefanakis et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Cassata et al., 2000; Etchberger et al., 2007; Kratsios et al., 2011; Stefanakis et al., 2015.

claim: cnd-1, a homolog of bHLH protein NeuroD, which is expressed transiently during the progenitor-like state in cholinergic MNs, is turned off normally in an unc-3 mutant.
source: Additionally, cnd-1, a homolog of bHLH protein NeuroD, which is expressed transiently during the progenitor-like state in cholinergic MNs, is turned off normally in an unc-3 mutant (Hallam et al., 2000; Kratsios et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hallam et al., 2000; Kratsios et al., 2011.

claim: In lin-11 mutants, expression of various terminal identity genes is reduced in ASG, but most tested markers are not completely eliminated.
source: In lin-11 mutants, for instance, expression of various terminal identity genes is reduced in ASG, but most tested markers are not completely eliminated (Sarafi-Reinach et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Sarafi-Reinach et al., 2001.

claim: In ttx-1 mutant AFD neurons, the expression of the glutamate transporter is off in only ~20% of neurons, while in a ceh-14; ttx-1 double mutant it is off or dim in ~80% of neurons.
source: Similarly, in ttx-1 mutant AFD neurons, the expression of the glutamate transporter is off in only ~20% of neurons, while in a ceh-14; ttx-1 double mutant it is off or dim in ~80% of neurons (Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013.

claim: The gcy-5fosmid::gfp locus is amenable to CHE-1 activation in both the ttx-1 single and ttx-1;ceh-14 double mutants to a similar extent.
source: However, the gcy-5fosmid::gfp locus is amenable to CHE-1 activation in both the ttx-1 single and ttx-1;ceh-14 double mutants to a similar extent.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: The loss of a terminal selector does not simply eliminate the differentiated state, rendering cells more plastic by default.
source: Hence, the loss of a terminal selector does not simply eliminate the differentiated state, rendering cells more plastic by default.
evidence: This is a key conclusion drawn from multiple lines of evidence.

claim: Terminal selectors trigger plasticity restriction by a pathway that can be partially decoupled from identity acquisition.
source: Rather, terminal selectors trigger plasticity restriction by a pathway that can be partially decoupled from identity acquisition.
evidence: This is a key conclusion of the study.

claim: Earlier acting selector genes of organ identity do not restrict cellular plasticity, as exemplified by the C. elegans pharyngeal organ selector pha-4.
source: Earlier acting selector genes of organ identity do not restrict cellular plasticity, as exemplified by the C. elegans pharyngeal organ selector pha-4 (Yuzyuk et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Yuzyuk et al., 2009.

claim: In all terminal selector mutants tested, CHE-1 activates ASE-identity genes in only about 30% of affected neurons.
source: In all terminal selector mutants tested, CHE-1 activates ASE-identity genes in only about 30% of affected neurons.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental data across multiple terminal selector mutants.

claim: Restriction of cellular plasticity requires input from terminal selector-independent factors.
source: This suggests that restriction of cellular plasticity also requires input from terminal selector-independent factors.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the incomplete penetrance of the phenotype in terminal selector mutants.

claim: Overall levels of H3K27me3 do not seem to be affected in somatic cells of L4 stage mes-2 mutants.
source: However, as overall levels of H3K27me3 do not seem to be affected in somatic cells of L4 stage mes-2 mutants (Bender et al., 2004), this would suggest that the lack or incorrect distribution of H3K27me3 in early stages of larval development is sufficient to interfere with restriction.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Bender et al., 2004.

claim: The lack or incorrect distribution of H3K27me3 in early stages of larval development is sufficient to interfere with restriction.
source: However, as overall levels of H3K27me3 do not seem to be affected in somatic cells of L4 stage mes-2 mutants (Bender et al., 2004), this would suggest that the lack or incorrect distribution of H3K27me3 in early stages of larval development is sufficient to interfere with restriction.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the mes-2 mutant data and citation to Bender et al., 2004.

claim: Somatic developmental defects have not yet been observed in H3K9 methyltransferase mutants in C. elegans.
source: However, in C. elegans, somatic developmental defects have not yet been observed in H3K9 methyltransferase mutants (Zeller et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Zeller et al., 2016.

claim: The current discovery that met-2 and the homologs of HP1 function to restrict plasticity highlights the utility of TF overexpression assays in uncovering mechanisms of development.
source: The current discovery that met-2 and the homologs of HP1 function to restrict plasticity highlights the utility of TF overexpression assays in uncovering mechanisms of development.
evidence: This is a concluding statement about the methodological contribution of the study.

claim: There is no obvious difference in the gross, overall levels of H3K9me3 between wildtype and unc-3 mutants in cholinergic MNs.
source: In cholinergic MNs there is no obvious difference in the gross, overall levels of H3K9me3 between wildtype and unc-3 mutants.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data.

claim: unc-3 does not seem to be playing a significant role in activating the expression of the met-2 or hpl-1/2 genes.
source: unc-3 does not seem to be playing a significant role in activating the expression of the met-2 or hpl-1/2 genes.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: unc-3 does not appear to regulate the distribution of H3K9me3 marks indirectly by controlling the deposition of positive marks (H3K4me3 and H3K36me3) at genes that it transcriptionally activates.
source: Moreover, unc-3 does not appear to regulate the distribution of H3K9me3 marks indirectly by controlling the deposition of positive marks (H3K4me3 and H3K36me3) at genes that it transcriptionally activates, since we find that the loss of enzymes that generate these marks does not promote cellular plasticity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: During identity specification, terminal selectors trigger a 'surveillance mechanism' which silences non-expressed, non-identity-specific genes.
source: Collectively, our data indicate that during identity specification, terminal selectors trigger a 'surveillance mechanism' which silences non-expressed, non-identity-specific genes.
evidence: This is a model proposed based on all the experimental data.

claim: The surveillance mechanism is likely to be mediated by met-2 and hpl-1/2 and carried out by the correct deposition of H3K9me on genes that are not activated in a given neuron type.
source: Genetic epistasis experiments suggest that this surveillance mechanism is (a) likely to be mediated by met-2 and hpl-1/2 and (b) carried out by the correct deposition of H3K9me on genes that are not activated in a given neuron type.
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the genetic epistasis data.

claim: Terminal selectors directly activate target genes that define a specific neuronal identity while also directly silencing genes that are normally not expressed in the respective neuron type.
source: One possibility is that terminal selectors directly activate target genes that define a specific neuronal identity while also directly silencing genes that are normally not expressed in the respective neuron type.
evidence: This is a hypothetical model discussed but disfavored by the authors.

claim: Heterochromatin forms, perhaps by default mechanisms, on loci that are not activated during cellular differentiation and unc-3 regulates the expression or function of some of the proteins that organize the heterochromatic state.
source: We rather favor at this point a model in which (a) heterochromatin forms, perhaps by default mechanisms, on loci that are not activated during cellular differentiation and (b) unc-3 regulates the expression or function of some of the proteins that organize the heterochromatic state (Figure 7).
evidence: This is the favored model proposed by the authors based on all the data.

claim: Broadly expressed heterochromatin regulators are 'plugged' into cell-specific differentiation program via their activation by cell-specific terminal selectors.
source: These organizers may be broadly expressed heterochromatin regulators that are 'plugged' into cell-specific differentiation program via their activation by cell-specific terminal selectors.
evidence: This is part of the proposed model.

claim: Such regulatory linkage would provide a checkpoint to coordinate the induction of cellular differentiation programs with the loss of cellular plasticity.
source: Such regulatory linkage would provide a checkpoint to coordinate the induction of cellular differentiation programs with the loss of cellular plasticity.
evidence: This is the proposed function of the regulatory mechanism.
